answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents can leverage unique hardware attestation. Each agent's identity is cryptographically tied to a distinct physical module, generating a signature as intricate as a yarrow leaf. Registering a new identity demands a secure computational burst, akin to a passing comet, proving control over this singular hardware. The cost for an attacker to flood the network with fake identities scales directly with the prohibitive expense of acquiring and maintaining truly unique physical hardware modules for each Sybil, stemming the tide of fraudulent entries.
